notes.text: The page is headed 'Une conjecture arithmético-géométrique', circled 9. It introduces a modular topos for relative smooth proper connected curves of genus g with marked disjoint sections, and lists the displayed small (g,nu) exceptions. In 'notion proche = schémable', only schémable remains a reading doubt after the main reader resolves the left words. The live source grammar de [crossed item] nu-uple is retained without repair.

It writes a natural homomorphism with a single circle on Autextlac and explains that the automorphisms do not exchange the classes of loops associated with the marked points. The tuple is followed by an arrow and le pt correspondant; the source's associee ending and the uncertain genus glyph are not reconciled mathematically.

The diagonal note asks whether one should be stricter and require commutation with written operations; it contains two literal colon-like point pairs, a large S_nu graph resolved by comparison with both occurrences on scan028, two question marks, and a request to examine g=0,nu=3, ending with four points. Its wording is transcribed as a marginal query, not a proved condition.

The second and third maps carry double circles. The following prose adds underlined stricts, a doubtful locale/lacets word and the identity on T=Tate(Qbar). The third map has analytic an superscripts and a short physical underbrace annotated by T_{g,nu} (Teichmüller). Its final claim begins 'dont on sait (théorie top.) que c'est un' and remains unfinished on this page.

Reader encoding decisions are literal: later basepoints remain j/xi, all three inner group graphs remain preferred Pi with pi alternatives, bars and an pairs are separate, the underbrace spans only the written middle portion, and no missing matching prose parenthesis or continuation is supplied. Each puncture list has a single horizontal continuation stroke; only the first map has a comma before its last x_nu. The overwritten prior modular capitals remain doubtful T-like graphs.

Limited integer check of the listed exceptions: with nonnegative integers g and nu, the inequality 2g-2+nu <= 0 gives nu <= 2 when g=0, nu=0 when g=1, and no solutions when g>=2. Thus its solution list is exactly the two groups of exceptions written here. This checks only that numerical list, not the assertions about an algebraic etendue, automorphisms or monodromy. It supplies no missing ink and does not resolve the separate g/0 genus reading.

Main adjudication preserves all four single continuation strokes and their individual comma patterns, the shortened brace, the canceled item above its equals sign, literal source grammar, and four visible insertion guides. Inner Pi/pi remains locally uncertain at all three occurrences; the two later basepoints remain j/xi. The terminal stroke after x_i is locally dash/period.
